analysis:
Both supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, covering lines 602-1057. They are documentation-only; no executable source, patch hunks or mode changes were supplied. The excerpts mainly describe v0.9.x release notes: App Attest recovery and serving authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058), legacy MDM/APNs coexistence (TB-009, T-036), durable build qualification and revocation (A-016, A-017, T-053, T-054), and fixed-time bounds on grants and receipts.

The notes consistently keep the security assumptions from the base threat model:
- App Attest remains independent of the legacy trust flags.
- Serving and MDM removal stay opt-in, and removal needs a fresh coordinator decision.
- Revocation fences stale grants.
- Every final inference handoff rechecks authorization.
- Unknown, missing or reported-only evidence never grants serving.
- Private-only providers are excluded from the public attestation roster (T-058). Public legacy SE keys remain linkable, and the notes say so.

No new attack surface or invalidated assumption is visible from the text alone. Examples of items I could not verify because the code is not in the batch: the claim that a 20-byte CandidateCDHash must uniquely match one durable, approved 32-byte CodeDirectory hash, and the claims that revocation fencing and the 30-second snapshot ceiling are enforced. The next pass should check those against the corresponding Go and Swift code (coordinator/appattest, registry/inference_authorization.go) if those files are part of the PR. Changelog claims are not evidence of implemented behavior. Findings: none.
